findings.reason: The protected Python solution generates all strobogrammatic numbers of length n using a center-outward recursive construction. Base cases handle length 0 ([""]) and length 1 (["0", "1", "8"]); for larger lengths, valid character pairs ("00", "11", "69", "88", "96") wrap around center strings of length n - 2, omitting "00" only for the outermost pair when length == n. The solution runs in O(n * 5^(n/2)) time and space; no candidate is required.

Building outward from valid center seeds and appending/prepending valid 180-degree rotation pairs guarantees that every generated string is strobogrammatic and has length n. Excluding leading zero pairs '00' at the outermost level prevents invalid numbers.
Generating 5^(n/2) strobogrammatic strings of length n takes O(n * 5^(n/2)) time and space. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts integer n, returning a list of strings containing all strobogrammatic numbers of length n without invalid leading zeros.

The approach accurately details center-outward recursive construction, base cases for even and odd lengths, leading-zero restriction for the outermost wrapper, and O(n * 5^(n/2)) time and space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover full n-digit brute-force enumeration, single-digit seeds, and internal zero-pair validity.
